From 24f8aba9a7c77c7e9d814a5754798e8346c7dd28 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan+linaro@kernel.org>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2023 17:43:25 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: qcom: sc7280: fix usb_2 wakeup interrupt types

The DP/DM wakeup interrupts are edge triggered and which edge to trigger
on depends on use-case and whether a Low speed or Full/High speed device
is connected.

Note that only triggering on rising edges can be used to detect resume
events but not disconnect events.

Fixes: bb9efa59c665 ("arm64: dts: qcom: sc7280: Add USB related nodes")
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan+linaro@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231120164331.8116-6-johan+linaro@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <andersson@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sc7280.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sc7280.dtsi
index a0f4e51d64c9..0153bace1cf7 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sc7280.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sc7280.dtsi
@@ -3469,8 +3469,8 @@ usb_2: usb@8cf8800 {
 			assigned-clock-rates = <19200000>, <200000000>;
 
 			interrupts-extended = <&intc GIC_SPI 240 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
-					      <&pdc 12 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>,
-					      <&pdc 13 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>;
+					      <&pdc 12 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH>,
+					      <&pdc 13 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH>;
 			interrupt-names = "hs_phy_irq",
 					  "dp_hs_phy_irq",
 					  "dm_hs_phy_irq";
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sc7280.dtsi`**
   - The interrupt types for the USB 2.0 wakeup interrupts have been changed from `IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING` to `IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH` for both `pdc 12` and `pdc 13`. This modification allows the system to detect both rising and falling edges, which is necessary for handling different use cases depending on the type of connected device (Low speed or Full/High speed).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in interrupt types is directly related to the functionality of detecting resume events and disconnect events for USB devices. By switching to `IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH`, the system can now properly handle wakeup interrupts for various device types, improving the robustness of USB connectivity on the sc7280 platform. This modification addresses the limitations of the previous implementation, which only detected rising edges, thus enhancing the overall performance and reliability of USB wakeup functionality.

The bug was caused by the incorrect configuration of the USB 2.0 wakeup interrupts, which were set to trigger only on rising edges (`IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING`).
